lessons.title: White-key note names

learn.title: Look at the black keys
learn.say: Black keys come in groups of 2 and groups of 3. Those groups are your map. C sits just LEFT of the group of 2. F sits just LEFT of the group of 3.
learn.tryText: Find a C. Play any C.
learn.hint: Look for a group of 2 black keys. C is the white key just to its left.

learn.title: Now F
learn.say: F is just left of the group of 3 black keys.
learn.tryText: Play any F.
learn.hint: Find a group of 3 black keys. F is the white key just to its left.

learn.title: Going up
learn.say: In music, we name notes with the letters A to G. That's the whole musical alphabet: just 7 letters. Moving to the RIGHT, the letters go up in order. Watch and listen.

learn.title: Going down
learn.say: Moving to the LEFT, the letters go backward: G F E D C B A. Watch and listen.

learn.title: G wraps back to A
learn.say: After G, the alphabet starts over at A. The keys repeat, so the same letters show up again higher up.

learn.title: All seven names
learn.say: Every white key has one of those seven names. The pattern of black keys repeats, so the names repeat too.
learn.tryText: Play any D.
learn.hint: D sits between the two black keys of the group of 2.

learn.title: One more
learn.say: Use the map: groups of 2 and 3 tell you where you are.
learn.tryText: Play any G.
learn.hint: Count from F: F, then G is the next white key to the right.

lessons.title: White-key triads
lessons.practice: Build triads on different white keys: play one, skip one, play one, skip one, play one. Watch the chord name and numeral change.

learn.title: Skip a key, play a key
learn.say: Play a white key, skip the next one, and play the one after it. That jump is called a third. Stack two thirds (play, skip, play, skip, play) and you get a triad: a chord made of 3 notes. The bottom note is the root, the middle note is the 3rd, and the top note is the 5th. A triad is named after its root.

learn.title: Build your own triads
learn.say: Pick any white key as the root. Play it, skip one, play one (the 3rd), skip one, play one (the 5th), all at the same time.
learn.tryText: Build 4 triads on white keys, each starting on a different key.
learn.hint: Root, skip a white key, 3rd, skip a white key, 5th. Hold all three down together.

learn.title: Chords in a key
learn.say: Build a triad on every white key from C up to B and you get the chords in the key of C major: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am and B°. The "m" means minor, a darker sound. B° (diminished) is the odd one out; it comes back later.

learn.title: Now F
learn.say: F is the root. Its 3rd is A and its 5th is C.
learn.tryText: Play an F triad.
learn.hint: Find an F and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: Now G
learn.say: G is the root. Its 3rd is B and its 5th is D.
learn.tryText: Play a G triad.
learn.hint: Find a G and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: A minor triad
learn.say: D is the root of D minor (Dm). Its 3rd is F and its 5th is A.
learn.tryText: Play D minor (Dm).
learn.hint: Find a D and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: Same keys, new home
learn.say: A minor uses the same white keys as C major, but A is home. Its chords are Am, B°, C, Dm, Em, F and G.

learn.title: Home in A minor
learn.say: A is the root of A minor (Am). Its 3rd is C and its 5th is E.
learn.tryText: Play A minor (Am).
learn.hint: Find an A and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: One more
learn.say: E is the root of E minor (Em). Its 3rd is G and its 5th is B.
learn.tryText: Play E minor (Em).
learn.hint: Find an E and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

lessons.title: Roman numerals
lessons.practice: Play the chords of C major and watch their Roman numerals. Try a loop like I – IV – V – I, or I – V – vi – IV.

learn.title: Chords get numbers
learn.say: Each triad in a key gets a Roman numeral for the scale note it is built on. Capital numerals (I, IV, V) are major. Lower-case numerals (ii, iii, vi) are minor. In C major: I = C, ii = Dm, iii = Em, IV = F, V = G, vi = Am, vii° = B°.

learn.title: Play the IV
learn.say: IV is built on the 4th note of the scale: count C, D, E, F.
learn.tryText: Play the IV chord in C.
learn.hint: Count up four from C: C (I), D (ii), E (iii), F (IV). Find an F and build the triad up from there.

learn.title: Play the vi
learn.say: vi is built on the 6th note of the scale, and it is minor.
learn.tryText: Play the vi chord in C.
learn.hint: The 6th note of C major is A. Find an A and build the triad up from there.

learn.title: Numerals tell a story
learn.say: Songs move from chord to chord. That pattern is called a progression. I – V – vi – IV is one of the most-used progressions in pop music. Listen to it in C major.

learn.title: Same numerals, new key
learn.say: Now the same I – V – vi – IV in G major: G, D, Em, C. The chords are different, but the pattern is the same. In both keys, I is home: the progression keeps coming back to it.

learn.title: Play the progression
learn.say: Play each chord, let go, then play the next.
learn.tryText: Play I – V – vi – IV in C, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In C: I = C, V = G, vi = Am, IV = F.

learn.title: Another favorite
learn.say: I – vi – IV – V is the sound of 1950s doo-wop and lots of songs since.
learn.tryText: Play I – vi – IV – V in C, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In C: I = C, vi = Am, IV = F, V = G.

learn.title: Numerals in A minor
learn.say: In a minor key the numerals count from the minor home chord. In A minor: i = Am, ii° = B°, III = C, iv = Dm, v = Em, VI = F, VII = G. Same white keys as C major, but now Am is home.

learn.title: A minor progression
learn.say: i – VI – III – VII is a favorite in minor keys: dark, then lifting.
learn.tryText: Play i – VI – III – VII in A minor, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In A minor: i = Am, VI = F, III = C, VII = G.

lessons.title: Black keys and half steps
lessons.practice: Find every black piano key and say both of its names. Then walk up the keyboard in half steps, black and white.

learn.title: Two names for one piano key
learn.say: Black piano keys are named after the white piano keys on either side of them: the one to the left or the one to the right, depending on the music. Sharp (♯) means one piano key higher. Flat (♭) means one piano key lower. The black piano key between C and D is C♯, and it is also D♭. Same piano key, two names.

learn.title: Find F♯
learn.say: F♯ is one piano key above F: the first black key of the group of 3.
learn.tryText: Play an F♯ (also called G♭).
learn.hint: Find F, then play the black piano key just to its right.

learn.title: Find B♭
learn.say: B♭ is one piano key below B: the last black key of the group of 3.
learn.tryText: Play a B♭ (also called A♯).
learn.hint: Find B, then play the black piano key just to its left.

learn.title: The smallest step
learn.say: A half step is a move to the very next piano key, up or down, black or white, with no skipping. E to F and B to C are half steps too: there is no black key between them.

learn.title: A half step up
learn.say: Up means to the right.
learn.tryText: Play the piano key a half step up from E.
learn.hint: There is no black key right of E, so the next piano key up is F.

learn.title: A half step down
learn.say: Down means to the left.
learn.tryText: Play the piano key a half step down from D.
learn.hint: The very next piano key left of D is the black key C♯ (D♭).

lessons.title: Major and minor chords anywhere
lessons.practice: Pick any piano key as a root. Count up 4 half steps, then 3 more: major. Count 3, then 4: minor. Listen to the difference.

learn.title: Major 3rd = 4 half steps
learn.say: A 3rd is the distance from a chord's root up to its 3rd. Count it in half steps: every piano key, black and white. A major 3rd is 4 half steps. From C: C♯, D, D♯, E. So C up to E is a major 3rd.

learn.title: Play major 3rds
learn.say: Pick any piano key. Count up 4 half steps and play both keys together.
learn.tryText: Play a major 3rd (4 half steps) on two different piano keys.
learn.hint: Count 4 half steps up from your bottom note, black keys included.

learn.title: Minor 3rd = 3 half steps
learn.say: A minor 3rd is one half step smaller: 3 half steps. From C: C♯, D, E♭. So C up to E♭ is a minor 3rd.

learn.title: Play minor 3rds
learn.say: Pick any piano key. Count up 3 half steps and play both keys together.
learn.tryText: Play a minor 3rd (3 half steps) on two different piano keys.
learn.hint: Count 3 half steps up from your bottom note, black keys included.

learn.title: D and Dm
learn.say: When we name a chord, we shorten it. A major chord is written with just its root letter: D major is "D". A minor chord adds a small "m": D minor is "Dm". So "C" means C major, and "Am" means A minor.

learn.title: Bright and dark
learn.say: Major chords sound bright. Minor chords sound darker. Listen: D, then Dm. Then A, then Am.

learn.title: Major = 4 + 3
learn.say: Stack the two 3rds to build a chord. Major: a major 3rd on the bottom (4 half steps), then a minor 3rd on top (3 more). C major: C, up 4 to E, up 3 to G.

learn.title: Minor = 3 + 4
learn.say: Minor flips it: a minor 3rd on the bottom (3 half steps), then a major 3rd on top (4 more). C minor: C, up 3 to E♭, up 4 to G. Only the middle note moves.

learn.title: D
learn.say: Count from D: up 4 to F♯, up 3 to A.
learn.tryText: Play D (D, F♯, A).
learn.hint: D, up 4 half steps is F♯ (a black key), up 3 more is A.

learn.title: Cm
learn.say: Count from C: up 3 to E♭, up 4 to G.
learn.tryText: Play Cm.
learn.hint: C, up 3 half steps is E♭, up 4 more is G.

learn.title: A
learn.say: Count from A: up 4, then up 3.
learn.tryText: Play A.
learn.hint: A, up 4 is C♯, up 3 more is E.

learn.title: Fm
learn.say: Count from F: up 3, then up 4.
learn.tryText: Play Fm.
learn.hint: F, up 3 is A♭, up 4 more is C.

lessons.title: Inversions
lessons.practice: Play a chord, then move its bottom note up an octave: same chord, new inversion. Then try moving between chords with as little motion as you can.

learn.title: Same chord, new bottom
learn.say: An inversion is the same chord with a different note on the bottom. Root position: the root is lowest (C E G). 1st inversion: the 3rd is lowest (E G C). 2nd inversion: the 5th is lowest (G C E).

learn.title: C, 1st inversion
learn.say: Put E on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play C major in 1st inversion (E on the bottom).
learn.hint: E, G, then the C above them.

learn.title: F, 2nd inversion
learn.say: Put the 5th (C) on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play F major in 2nd inversion (C on the bottom).
learn.hint: C, then F and A above it.

learn.title: G, 1st inversion
learn.say: Put the 3rd (B) on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play G major in 1st inversion.
learn.hint: B, D, then the G above them.

learn.title: Move as little as possible
learn.say: Good players move between chords with as little motion as they can. C to F: keep C, move E up to F and G up to A. C to G: keep G, move C down to B and E down to D.

learn.title: Your turn
learn.say: From C (C E G), the smoothest F keeps C on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play F with C on the bottom (C, F, A).
learn.hint: Keep your thumb on C. Move the other two fingers up one white key each.

lessons.title: Chord rhythms
lessons.practice: Turn on the metronome and play one chord in different rhythms: whole notes, half notes, quarters, 8ths. Then try the tresillo: 1, the + of 2, and 4.

learn.title: Whole notes
learn.say:
A whole note lasts the whole bar: 4 beats.
Play on 1 and hold it through 2, 3 and 4.
Press ▶ Listen and count along.

learn.title: Half notes
learn.say:
A half note lasts 2 beats, so two fit in a bar.
Play on 1 and on 3.

learn.title: Quarter notes
learn.say:
A quarter note lasts 1 beat: play on every count, 1 2 3 4.
This is the beat you tap your foot to.

learn.title: Play quarter notes
learn.say:
C for a bar, then F for a bar, on every beat.
Press ▶ Play along: 4 clicks count you in.
learn.tryText: Play C, then F, in quarter notes.

learn.title: 8th notes
learn.say:
8th notes split every beat in two.
Count 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ("one and two and…").
Play on every number AND every +.

learn.title: Play 8th notes
learn.say:
Small, quick moves: keep your hand on the chord and bounce.
Count out loud: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 +.
learn.tryText: Play C, then F, in 8th notes.

learn.title: Off the beat
learn.say:
Now the chord comes only on the +s (the upbeats), short, never on the numbers.
Keep the numbers going in your head (or tap your foot on them) and play in the gaps.
It is the sound of reggae and ska.

learn.title: Play off the beat
learn.say: Tap your foot on 1 2 3 4. Play only when your foot comes up.
learn.tryText: Play C, then F, on the +s only.

learn.title: The tresillo
learn.say:
The tresillo ("little three") groups 8 eighths as 3 + 3 + 2.
Play on 1, on the + of 2, and on 4.
It is the 3 side of the son clave from Cuba, and it drives countless pop, Latin, reggaeton and R&B songs.

learn.title: Play the tresillo
learn.say:
Count 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + and play on 1, the + of 2, and 4.
Or think of it as long, long, short.
learn.tryText: Play C, then G, in the tresillo rhythm.

learn.title: Oom-pah
learn.say:
Break the chord up: the root alone on 1 and 3, the chord on 2 and 4.
Oom-pah, oom-pah: the bass and the chord take turns.
The "pah" can be the whole chord, or just its 3rd and 5th.

learn.title: Play oom-pah
learn.say: Root, chord, root, chord. (For the chord, the 3rd and 5th alone are fine too.)
learn.tryText: Play C, then G: root on 1 and 3, chord on 2 and 4.

learn.title: Split hands
learn.say:
Now spread it out: the left hand plays the root low, the right hand plays the chord up high.
C is C E G. G is played as D G B (its 2nd inversion, from Lesson 6), so your right hand barely moves.
That is how a lot of piano accompaniment sounds.

learn.title: Play split hands
learn.say:
Left hand: the root, low. Right hand: the chord, high.
For G, use the inversion D G B up high (2nd inversion).
learn.tryText: Play C, then G: low root on 1 and 3, the chord up high on 2 and 4 (G as D G B).

learn.title: Round the triad
learn.say:
An arpeggio plays the chord one note at a time.
Go round and round the triad in 8th notes: C E G C E G C E, then A C E A C E A C.
Three notes in a pattern of eight: it rolls over the bar.

learn.title: Play the triad round and round
learn.say: Fingers 1 3 5 on C E G, then on A C E. Keep going round.
learn.tryText: Play C E G C E G C E, then A C E A C E A C.

learn.title: Up to the octave
learn.say:
Now go up the chord to the root an octave higher: root, 3rd, 5th, octave.
In 8th notes that is two runs up per bar.
It is the flowing sound of piano ballads.

learn.title: Play an arpeggio
learn.say:
Fingers 1 2 3 5 on C E G C, then on A C E A.
One note per 8th, smooth and even.
learn.tryText: Play C, then Am, as arpeggios in 8th notes.

lessons.title: Bass lines
lessons.practice: Play just the root of each chord, low, with your left hand. Then try the styles: rock 8ths, root and 5th, octaves, off-beats, a trap 808, passing notes into the next chord.

learn.title: The bass plays the root
learn.say:
The bass holds the band together: it plays the root of each chord, low.
Pop and ballads keep it simple: the root on the beat.

learn.title: Play roots on the beat
learn.say: C for a bar, then F. Use your left hand.
learn.tryText: Play the roots, C then F, on every beat.

learn.title: Rock: pump the root
learn.say: Rock bass drives: the root in steady 8th notes, like an engine.

learn.title: Play rock 8ths
learn.say: Keep it even and steady: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 +.
learn.tryText: Pump the root in 8th notes: C, then F.

learn.title: Root and 5th
learn.say:
Country, folk and early rock and roll: the root on 1, held, then the 5th on beat 4 leading into the next bar.
The 5th is the top note of the triad: C to G, F to C.

learn.title: Play root and 5th
learn.say: Root on 1 (hold it), the 5th on 4.
learn.tryText: Play the root on 1 and the 5th on 4: C then G, F then C.

learn.title: Octaves
learn.say: Disco and dance music bounce between the root and the root an octave up, in 8th notes.

learn.title: Play octaves
learn.say: Thumb on the low root, pinky on the high one, rock between them.
learn.tryText: Bounce between the root and its octave in 8th notes.

learn.title: Root, octave, 5th
learn.say:
Now space it out: the root on 1, the octave on the + of 2, then the 5th on 4.
The 5th adds a little lift that leads into the next chord.

learn.title: Play root, octave, 5th
learn.say: Root on 1, the octave on the + of 2, the 5th on 4.
learn.tryText: Play root, octave, 5th: C, then F.

learn.title: Trap: the 808
learn.say:
Trap bass is the 808: a long, low, booming note, and the kick drum hits with every one.
The beat is fast (140), but each chord lasts two bars: few notes, held long, off the beat. The jump to the octave adds bounce.
The hi-hats do the fast stuff, so the bass doesn't have to.

learn.title: Play an 808 line
learn.say: Root on 1, root on 4, then the octave on 2 of the next bar. Hold each note for its whole length.
learn.tryText: Play the 808 line: root, root, octave, two bars for each chord.

learn.title: Passing notes
learn.say:
A bass line doesn't have to jump from root to root.
Hold the root, then on beat 4 play one passing note that leads into the next chord.
G to C: B is right below C.
C to Em: D steps up to E.
Em to D: E♭ slides down a half step into D.

learn.title: Play passing notes
learn.say: Hold each root, then the passing note on 4: G … B, C … D, E … E♭, then D.
learn.tryText: Play G, C, E and D, with B, D and E♭ on beat 4 to lead into the next one.

learn.title: Reggaeton: the tresillo
learn.say:
Reggaeton and lots of Latin pop put the bass on the tresillo from Lesson 7: 1, the + of 2, and 4.
Each hit climbs the chord: the root, then the 5th, then the octave.

lessons.title: Riffs and melodies
lessons.practice: Put on a groove in the Jam Room, turn on Key lock with Pentatonic, and make up a riff: start with one note and a rhythm, then add a second note, then a third.

learn.title: One-note riff
learn.say:
A riff is a short tune that repeats, like a guitar riff or a synth hook.
Start with ONE note. The rhythm is what makes it a riff.

learn.title: Play a one-note riff
learn.say: Just A: long, long, short.
learn.tryText: Play the one-note riff on A.

learn.title: Two-note riff
learn.say:
Add a second note: C, three half steps up.
Two notes and a rhythm already sound like a song.

learn.title: Play a two-note riff
learn.say: A, A, C, A.
learn.tryText: Play the two-note riff: A and C.

learn.title: Three-note riff
learn.say: A third note: D. Go up and come back home.

learn.title: Play a three-note riff
learn.say: A, C, D, C, A.
learn.tryText: Play the three-note riff: A, C and D.

learn.title: The pentatonic scale
learn.say:
Those notes come from the minor pentatonic scale: A C D E G.
Five notes that sound good over every chord in A minor.
Riffs and solos in rock, blues, pop and hip hop live here.

learn.title: Play the pentatonic
learn.say: Up from A to A, then back down to E.
learn.tryText: Play the A minor pentatonic up and back down.

learn.title: The blue note
learn.say:
Add one note between D and E: D♯ (or E♭). It is the blue note.
Slide through it on the way to E; don't sit on it.

learn.title: Call and response
learn.say:
Melodies talk. Bar 1 asks a question: it climbs and stops up high, unfinished.
Bar 2 answers: it comes back home to A.

learn.title: Play call and response
learn.say: Up A C D E (the question), then D C A (the answer).
learn.tryText: Play the call, then the response.

learn.title: Land on a chord tone
learn.say:
End a phrase on a note of the chord that is playing and it sounds finished.
Over Am that is A, C or E. Over F it is F, A or C.
Here both phrases land on C, which is in both chords.

learn.title: Make your own
learn.say:
Now make your own riff in the Jam Room.
Pick a groove, then turn on Key lock and choose Pentatonic: every key you can play will fit.
Start with one note and a rhythm. Then add a second note. Then a third.

lessons.title: Major scales
lessons.practice: Play the major scales of C, G, D and F, up and down. Use the fingering: tuck your thumb under, never run out of fingers.

learn.title: Whole and half steps
learn.say: A major scale climbs 8 notes, from one letter to the same letter an octave up. It always uses the same pattern of steps: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. A whole step is 2 half steps. C major uses only the white keys: C D E F G A B C.

learn.title: Fingers
learn.say:
Number your right-hand fingers: thumb = 1, pinky = 5.
Up: C D E with 1 2 3, thumb under to F, then G A B C with 2 3 4 5.
Down: the same fingers, and finger 3 crosses over the thumb to E.

learn.title: Play C major
learn.say:
Up: 1 2 3, thumb under, 1 2 3 4 5.
Down: 5 4 3 2 1, 3 over the thumb, 2 1.
learn.tryText: Play the C major scale up and back down: C to C, then down to C.
learn.hint: C D E F G A B C, all white keys.

learn.title: G major: one sharp
learn.say: Start a scale on G and keep the same pattern of whole and half steps. To make the last step a half step, F has to become F♯. So G major has one sharp: F♯. The fingering is the same as C major, up and down.

learn.title: Play G major
learn.say: Remember the F♯.
learn.tryText: Play the G major scale up and back down.
learn.hint: G A B C D E F♯ G.

learn.title: D major: two sharps
learn.say: Start on D and keep the same pattern. This time two notes have to move up: F becomes F♯ and C becomes C♯. So D major has two sharps. Fingering: 1 2 3, thumb under, 1 2 3 4 5, and the same coming down.

learn.title: Play D major
learn.say: Two black keys this time.
learn.tryText: Play the D major scale up and back down.
learn.hint: D E F♯ G A B C♯ D.

learn.title: F major: one flat
learn.say:
Some scales use flats instead: F, B♭, E♭, A♭ and more.
In F major the 4th note must be a half step above A, so B becomes B♭ (each letter is used once, so not A♯).
Fingers: 1 2 3 4 on F G A B♭, thumb under to C; coming down, 4 crosses over the thumb.

learn.title: Play F major
learn.say: Remember the B♭.
learn.tryText: Play the F major scale up and back down.
learn.hint: F G A B♭ C D E F.

lessons.title: 7th chords
lessons.practice: Add a 4th note to your triads: one more 3rd on top. Try G7 going to C, and Dm7 – G7 – Cmaj7. Watch the chord names change.

learn.title: One more 3rd
learn.say: A 7th chord is a triad with one more 3rd stacked on top. That top note is the 7th: seven letters up from the root. G7 is G, B, D and F.

learn.title: Play G7
learn.say: Hold all four notes together.
learn.tryText: Play G7 (G, B, D, F).
learn.hint: Build a G triad (G B D), then add F on top.

learn.title: Find the 7th from the octave
learn.say:
You know the octave: G up to the next G.
A major 7th is a half step below the octave: G up to F♯.
A minor 7th is a whole step below the octave: G up to F.
Find the octave first, then step down.

learn.title: Play major 7ths
learn.say: Pick a root. Find the octave above it, then step down a half step (one piano key). Play the root and that note together.
learn.tryText: Play a major 7th on three different roots.
learn.hint: Find the octave, then go down one piano key.

learn.title: Play minor 7ths
learn.say: Pick a root. Find the octave above it, then step down a whole step (two piano keys). Play the root and that note together.
learn.tryText: Play a minor 7th on three different roots.
learn.hint: Find the octave, then go down two piano keys.

learn.title: Major, dominant and minor 7ths
learn.say:
Three kinds of 7th chord, all on G:
Gmaj7 (major 7th chord) = major triad + major 7th (F♯). It sounds dreamy.
G7 (dominant 7th chord) = major triad + minor 7th (F). It wants to move home.
Gm7 (minor 7th chord) = minor triad + minor 7th (F). It sounds smooth.

learn.title: Play major 7th chords
learn.say:
Major triad + major 7th (a half step below the octave).
Cmaj7 = C E G B. Fmaj7 = F A C E. Gmaj7 = G B D F♯.
learn.tryText: Play Cmaj7, Fmaj7 and Gmaj7, one after another.

learn.title: Major 7ths with black keys
learn.say:
Dmaj7, Emaj7 and Amaj7 all have the same shape: white, black, white, black.
Dmaj7 = D F♯ A C♯. Emaj7 = E G♯ B D♯. Amaj7 = A C♯ E G♯.
Learn the shape once and slide it.
learn.tryText: Play Dmaj7, Emaj7 and Amaj7, one after another.

learn.title: Play minor 7th chords
learn.say:
Minor triad + minor 7th (a whole step below the octave).
Dm7 = D F A C. Em7 = E G B D. Am7 = A C E G.
learn.tryText: Play Dm7, Em7 and Am7, one after another.

learn.title: Minor 7ths with black keys
learn.say:
Same recipe, starting on other notes.
Bm7 = B D F♯ A. F♯m7 = F♯ A C♯ E. Gm7 = G B♭ D F.
learn.tryText: Play Bm7, F♯m7 and Gm7, one after another.

learn.title: Play dominant 7th chords
learn.say:
Major triad + minor 7th (a whole step below the octave).
G7 = G B D F. C7 = C E G B♭. D7 = D F♯ A C.
learn.tryText: Play G7, C7 and D7, one after another.

learn.title: Dominant 7ths with black keys
learn.say:
A7 = A C♯ E G (like Amaj7, but the 7th steps down to G).
F7 = F A C E♭ (like Fmaj7, but E becomes E♭).
learn.tryText: Play A7, then F7.

learn.title: The 7th chords of C major
learn.say: Stack four notes on every white key and you get the 7th chords of C major: Cmaj7, Dm7, Em7, Fmaj7, G7, Am7 and Bø7. Their numerals add the 7: Imaj7, ii7, iii7, IVmaj7, V7, vi7 and viiø7.

learn.title: ii7 – V7 – Imaj7
learn.say: ii7 – V7 – Imaj7 is the most famous progression in jazz. In C it is Dm7, G7, Cmaj7. Move each finger as little as you can.

learn.title: Play ii7 – V7 – Imaj7
learn.say: Play each chord, let go, then play the next.
learn.tryText: Play ii7 – V7 – Imaj7 in C, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In C: ii7 = Dm7, V7 = G7, Imaj7 = Cmaj7.
